findings.message: `list_paths` reads `git ls-tree -r --name-only` without `-z`. With the default `core.quotePath`, git prints any path with non-ASCII bytes, a tab, a quote or a backslash as a C-quoted string, for example `".specclaw/changes/065-caf\303\251/follow-ups.md"`. That string never matches `LIST_RE`, so the list is skipped and its items are neither listed nor gated. This is the same raw-path defect this PR fixed in `_final_pass_drift` with `-z` (the AC-1 test with `.specclaw/é.md`), but the second git path reader was not fixed. Fix: use `ls-tree -r -z --full-name --name-only` and split on `\0`. Add a variant test with a non-ASCII change directory and a quote or tab in a path.
findings.scenario: A target commit adds `.specclaw/changes/065-café/follow-ups.md` containing `- [major S1] ... <!-- fp:abc class:security -->`. `specclaw-sync release base target` prints `0 open item(s)` and exits 0, where it should list the item and exit 1.

findings.message: The comment says that running after the bookkeeping push means "the iteration checked is the head policy sees". Azure DevOps creates the iteration for a push asynchronously, and GitHub's `headRefOid` in `specclaw-pr` can also lag just after a push. The status can therefore land on the previous iteration or SHA and then be dropped by "reset on source update". The result fails closed (no status, no false approval), but the comment overstates the guarantee. Either poll briefly until the iteration or head SHA equals the locally pushed `git rev-parse HEAD`, or reword the comment and point to the CI template as the reliable poster.

The `targetUrl` (and the GitHub `target_url` in `specclaw-pr` and `ci/github-actions.yml`) is built from the branch name and round path by plain string interpolation, with no URL encoding. A branch name containing `&`, `#` or `%`, all valid in git, yields a broken link. Encode the components, for example with `urllib.parse.quote`, since Python is already invoked to build the body.

The two templates handle a failed status POST differently. The Azure step runs under `set -e`, so a failed POST fails the step. The GitHub step uses `set -uo pipefail` without `-e` and relies on the `if` branch's last command for its exit status. Any command added after `gh api` would hide the failure. Make the GitHub status step fail explicitly on a failed `gh api` (or add `-e`), so a status that was not posted is never shown as a green step.
